entries.sentence: Many people with iron deficiency anaemia have only a few symptoms.
entries.note: NHS summary: many people have few symptoms.

entries.sentence: Tiredness and a lack of energy are common, and some people also notice shortness of breath, a pounding heartbeat, paler skin or headaches.
entries.note: Summary listed tiredness, shortness of breath, palpitations, paler skin, headaches.

entries.sentence: Less often there may be ringing in the ears, an altered sense of taste, hair loss, a craving to eat non-food items (called pica) or spoon-shaped nails.
entries.note: Summary listed tinnitus, altered taste, hair loss, pica, spoon-shaped nails as less common.

entries.sentence: Low iron has also been linked with restless legs syndrome, even when anaemia is not fully present.
entries.note: Search summary linked restless legs to low iron even without full anaemia; page attribution not certain.

entries.sentence: Vitamin B12 or folate deficiency anaemia can cause extreme tiredness, a sore red tongue, pins and needles and mouth ulcers.
entries.note: NHS symptoms page list.

entries.sentence: It can also cause muscle weakness and problems with vision, memory or judgement.
entries.note: NHS symptoms page list.

entries.sentence: The NHS says that the longer this type goes untreated, the higher the chance of permanent damage, and long-term B12 deficiency can damage nerves.
entries.note: Summary: longer untreated, higher chance of permanent damage; long-term B12 deficiency can cause nerve damage (attribution to specific page not certain).

entries.sentence: Iron deficiency is the most common type of anaemia, and vitamin B12 and folate deficiency are other frequent causes.
entries.note: MedlinePlus: iron deficiency is the most common type; summary named B12 and folate as other frequent causes.

entries.sentence: MedlinePlus also lists anaemia of chronic disease, sickle cell anaemia, thalassaemia and aplastic anaemia among the types.
entries.note: MedlinePlus lists these types.

entries.sentence: Anaemia of chronic disease is linked with long-term conditions such as kidney disease, cancer, ulcerative colitis or rheumatoid arthritis.
entries.note: StatPearls summary listed these associated conditions.

entries.sentence: Thalassaemia is inherited, while aplastic anaemia involves damage to the stem cells in the bone marrow that make blood cells.
entries.note: StatPearls summary: thalassaemia inherited via gene changes; aplastic anaemia destruction of haematopoietic stem cells.

entries.sentence: In the UK, the most common cause of vitamin B12 deficiency is pernicious anaemia.
entries.note: Summary of NHS pages: most common cause in the UK is pernicious anaemia.

entries.sentence: In this condition the immune system attacks healthy cells in the stomach, so the body cannot absorb B12 from food.
entries.note: Summary: immune system attacks healthy stomach cells, preventing B12 absorption.

entries.sentence: Diet can also contribute, particularly for vegetarians, and some medicines, including anticonvulsants and proton pump inhibitors, can reduce absorption.
entries.note: Summary: diet and medicines such as anticonvulsants and PPIs; vegetarians named in StatPearls-type summary.

entries.sentence: Folate deficiency can also follow heavy alcohol use or a raised need for folate, as in pregnancy.
entries.note: Summary: folate deficiency from alcohol use disorder or increased demand such as pregnancy.

entries.sentence: A GP usually asks about lifestyle and medical history and then arranges a blood test.
entries.note: Summary: GP asks about lifestyle and history, usually does a blood test.

entries.sentence: This is a full blood count, which checks the red blood cells, and the GP may also test ferritin, a protein that stores iron.
entries.note: Summary: full blood count; ferritin is a protein that stores iron.

entries.sentence: A low ferritin suggests that there is not much iron stored in the body.
entries.note: Summary: low ferritin suggests little iron stored.

entries.sentence: Finding the cause matters because treatment depends on it.
entries.note: Summary: finding the cause matters as treatment depends on it.

entries.sentence: The GP may ask about diet, heavy periods and medicines such as ibuprofen or aspirin, which can cause bleeding in the stomach.
entries.note: Summary of NHS page.

entries.sentence: In men and in women after the menopause, bleeding in the gut is the most common cause of iron deficiency, whereas in women before the menopause it is heavy periods.
entries.note: Summary of NHS page; page attribution not fully certain.

entries.sentence: If the cause is unclear, further tests may follow, such as a stool sample test for blood, and testing for coeliac disease may be suggested.
entries.note: Summary: faecal immunochemical test; coeliac screening noted (one hospital leaflet); NHS page attribution uncertain.

entries.sentence: For vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, a GP can often make the diagnosis from symptoms and blood tests.
entries.note: Summary: GP can often diagnose from symptoms and blood tests; NHS diagnosis page.

entries.sentence: Treatment depends on the type of anaemia and its cause.
entries.note: Summary: treatment depends on the cause.

entries.sentence: Iron deficiency anaemia is usually treated with iron tablets and iron-rich foods, while the underlying cause, such as heavy periods or bleeding, is also addressed.
entries.note: Summary of NHS page.

entries.sentence: Common side effects of iron tablets include constipation or diarrhoea, tummy pain, heartburn, feeling sick and darker than usual poo.
entries.note: Summary listed these side effects.

entries.sentence: Taking tablets with or shortly after food can help, and the GP may change how often they are taken.
entries.note: Summary: with or after food helps; GP may adjust frequency.

entries.sentence: An iron infusion may be used when a person cannot take tablets or cannot absorb iron through the gut.
entries.note: Summary: infusion if unable to take tablets or absorb iron.

entries.sentence: Vitamin B12 deficiency is usually treated with hydroxocobalamin injections, followed by tablets or continuing injections depending on the cause.
entries.note: NHS treatment page summary.

entries.sentence: When the deficiency is not caused by diet, injections may be needed long term.
entries.note: Summary: injections typically continuing if not diet-related.

entries.sentence: Folate deficiency is treated with folic acid tablets, and doctors check B12 first because folic acid can sometimes hide a B12 deficiency.
entries.note: Summary of NHS treatment page.

entries.sentence: A follow-up blood test is usually arranged to confirm that treatment is working.
entries.note: Summary: another blood test to confirm treatment success.

entries.sentence: For other types, MedlinePlus says anaemia usually improves when the condition causing it is treated.
entries.note: MedlinePlus via summary.

entries.sentence: Vitamin B12 is found in meat, fish, eggs, dairy products and fortified foods.
entries.note: Summary of diet sources.

entries.sentence: Good sources of folate include broccoli, brussels sprouts, asparagus, peas, chickpeas and brown rice.
entries.note: Summary of diet sources.

entries.sentence: Iron supplements should be kept out of the reach of children, because an overdose in a young child can be fatal.
entries.note: Summary of NHS safety note.

entries.sentence: Untreated iron deficiency anaemia may lead to heart problems, complications in pregnancy and delayed development in children.
entries.note: NHLBI and NHS summary of complications.

entries.sentence: Delays in treating B12 deficiency can cause lasting nerve damage, so early diagnosis matters.
entries.note: Summary: treatment delays can cause irreversible neurological damage.

entries.sentence: Vitamin B12 deficiency anaemia most often responds well to treatment.
entries.note: StatPearls summary.

entries.sentence: Sickle cell disease causes long-term anaemia with episodes of pain, and care focuses on managing symptoms and preventing complications.
entries.note: Summary: chronic haemolytic anaemia and pain episodes; treatment aims.

entries.sentence: Overall, the outlook depends on the condition causing the anaemia.
entries.note: MedlinePlus: outlook depends on the cause.

entries.sentence: Chest pain, fainting or severe breathlessness at rest need an emergency call to 999, black or bloody stools need NHS 111 or a same-day GP call, and ongoing tiredness or paleness is a reason for a routine GP appointment.
entries.note: Routes to care; consistent with the page's existing seekCare, not from retrieved text.

entries.sentence: No, iron deficiency is only the most common type.
entries.note: MedlinePlus: most common type.

entries.sentence: Anaemia can also come from vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, long-term conditions, inherited conditions such as sickle cell disease and thalassaemia, or aplastic anaemia.
entries.note: Types list.

entries.sentence: Treatment depends on the type, which is why a blood test comes first.
entries.note: Summary: blood test; treatment depends on cause.

entries.sentence: Finding the cause matters because treatment depends on it.
entries.note: Summary of NHS page.

entries.sentence: In men and in women after the menopause, bleeding in the gut is the most common cause.
entries.note: Summary of NHS page.

entries.sentence: Causes such as stomach ulcers or bowel cancer are considered, so a GP may arrange further tests if the reason is unclear.
entries.note: Summary: ulcers and bowel cancer considered; further tests if unclear.

entries.sentence: They can, and the NHS lists constipation or diarrhoea, tummy pain, heartburn, feeling sick and darker than usual poo.
entries.note: Summary listed these.

entries.sentence: Taking them with or shortly after food can help.
entries.note: Summary.

entries.sentence: A GP may adjust how often the tablets are taken, and people with troublesome effects usually talk to the GP rather than stopping on their own.
entries.note: Summary: GP may advise fewer tablets or alternate days; NHS also said keep taking despite side effects.

entries.sentence: Injections are used when the problem is poor absorption, as in pernicious anaemia, where the immune system attacks healthy stomach cells.
entries.note: Summary: pernicious anaemia prevents absorption; injections if not diet-related.

entries.sentence: The NHS says hydroxocobalamin is the form used in the UK.
entries.note: Summary: hydroxocobalamin preferred in UK.

entries.sentence: When low B12 is only due to diet, tablets may be enough.
entries.note: Summary: diet-related deficiency may use daily tablets.

entries.sentence: No, many people with iron deficiency anaemia have only a few symptoms.
entries.note: Summary.

entries.sentence: It can be found through a blood test done for another reason.
entries.note: Common knowledge; consistent with existing page.

entries.sentence: Anyone who has symptoms such as persistent tiredness, paleness or breathlessness can book a routine GP appointment.
entries.note: Routine route to care; not from retrieved text.
